column2: Vidi: Large Multimodal Models for Video Understanding and Editing
column3: Vidi Team; Celong Liu; Chia-Wen Kuo; et al.
column9: Video up to >1 h at 1 fps visual + 16 kHz audio, plus text query (keyword/phrase/sentence)
column10: Time ranges matching the query (temporal retrieval); not query-free clip selection
column11: Synthetic video/audio with GT ranges, then real video with timestamp+caption/ASR pairs, then TR post-training that mirrors the VUE-TR benchmark
column12: Released: VUE-TR benchmark (1,598 queries / 428 videos / ~107 h; 20 s to >1 h; vision, audio and mixed queries)
column15: AUC of temporal precision / recall / IoU
column16: Overall IoU-AUC 39.6 (Vidi-1.5) / 35.4 (Vidi-7B) vs Gemini-2.0-Flash 21.2, Gemini-2.5-Pro 15.2, GPT-4o 13.6; audio-query accuracy lower than vision-query for all models
column17: Yes: github.com/bytedance/vidi (Vidi-1.5-9B weights + finetune code per README)
column18: GitHub license field NOASSERTION; no LICENSE file found [V]
column21: Strong long-video timestamp grounding with audio; but it solves query->moment retrieval, has no engagement or self-containedness notion, and reports no clip-extraction numbers.

column2: QVHighlights: Detecting Moments and Highlights in Videos via Natural Language Queries
column3: Jie Lei; Tamara L. Berg; Mohit Bansal
column11: Human annotation (queries, moments, saliency); weak pretraining with ASR captions
column12: Released: >10,000 YouTube videos (avg ~150 s per SVHighlights/Repurpose tables)
column16: abstract: ASR-caption weak pretraining 'substantially' improves Moment-DETR (numbers not read here)
column21: Foundational query-based benchmark (human saliency); too short and query-driven to match our setting, cited as baseline family by Repurpose-10K/SVHighlights.

column2: PodReels: Human-AI Co-Creation of Video Podcast Teasers
column3: Sitong Wang; Zheng Ning; Anh Truong et al.
column9: Podcast transcript + diarization + audio events + user parameters (length 15/30/45s, speakers, style, keywords)
column10: Candidate single-moment teasers (sentence IDs -> timestamps) with taglines; transcript refinement UI with context windows
column11: Formative study of audience comments and 5 creator interviews; no trained labels (GPT-4 zero-shot)
column12: 4 episodes technical eval (168 single-param + 30 multi-param clips)
column16: Names 'clear context' (self-contained; avoid out-of-context 'here'/'them') as a design principle; no automatic self-containedness check; user study time 9.9 vs 16.7 min, outcome 5.6 vs 4.1 (1-7)
column21: [CORE] Earliest HCI statement that teasers must be self-contained and hooky, with context handled by human review UI rather than a metric

column2: Mr. HiSum: A Large-scale Dataset for Video Highlight Detection and Summarization
column9: YouTube-8M video (1 fps Inception-v3 features, <=300 s)
column10: frame importance scores -> highlight shots / summary
column12: 31,892 videos (YT-8M subset; music category, deleted videos and >300 s excluded)
column16: user study 25 videos/30 annotators: 64.8% of clips agree with Most-replayed label, 19.6% disagree, 15.6% neutral; models trained on Mr.HiSum beat in-domain training on TVSum/SumMe F1
column17: yes: github.com/MRHiSum/MR.HiSum (labels, KTS change points, gtsummary; features must be rebuilt)
column18: CC BY 4.0 (per repo README) + YouTube ToS
column21: [CORE] Authors themselves flag partial-replay ambiguity and 'self-fulfilling' bias (UI shows heatmap after >=50k views; cannot be separated); no position/intro/title/channel analysis found in the main text

column2: Rhapsody: A Dataset for Highlight Detection in Podcasts
column9: podcast audio + WhisperX transcript (+HuBERT/DVA audio embeddings)
column11: YouTube replay graph: top-K (K=20) segments with score>0.5; first segment value set to second value to correct start-of-video bias
column15: hit rate, precision, recall, F1, AP
column16: Sec 2.2: before correction 75% of episodes had a highlight at the first segment; after, avg highlights/episode 5.86->5.20; best system (fine-tuned Llama-3.2-1B text+HuBERT) hit rate 0.490, P 0.266, F1 0.197 vs random 0.220/0.053/0.039
column17: yes: github.com/younghanstark/rhapsody (video IDs, replay graphs, processed features; no audio)
column21: [CORE] Closest domain match (long, speech-first, replay-derived labels) and one of only two papers that explicitly correct a Most-Replayed artifact - but fix is a one-bin heuristic, no propensity/title/channel treatment
